questions.q: The First Buddhist Council was held in which year and at which place?

questions.q: Which ruler organized the Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra?

questions.q: Who established the Nanda dynasty by ending the Shishunaga dynasty, assuming the title 'Ekarat'?

questions.q:

questions.q: Which Greek ambassador wrote 'Indica' describing the Mauryan empire?

questions.q: In the Kalinga War (261 BC) which Major Rock Edict of Ashoka describes the war?

questions.q: Who established Nalanda University during the Gupta period?
questions.explanation: Nalanda University was established during the reign of Kumaragupta I (415-455 AD). It later became the greatest centre of Buddhist education.

questions.q: Who was the founder of the Pala dynasty, and which ruler founded Vikramshila University?
questions.explanation: Gopala founded the Pala dynasty in 750 AD (and Odantapuri University). His son Dharmapala founded Vikramshila University at Bhagalpur.

questions.q: Which ruler destroyed Nalanda and Vikramshila universities and conquered Bihar Sharif (Odantapuri) in 1198 AD?

questions.q: Who was the founder of the Karnat dynasty of Mithila, with its capital at Simraongarh?
questions.explanation: The Karnat dynasty of Mithila-Tirhut was founded by Nanyadeva, with its capital at Simraongarh (now in Nepal). Harisimhadeva was its last ruler.

questions.q: Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun at which two battles to establish the Sur dynasty?
questions.explanation: Sher Khan defeated Humayun at Chausa in 1539 AD (taking the title Sher Shah) and at Kannauj (Bilgram) in 1540 AD, establishing the Sur dynasty in Delhi.

questions.q: Which silver and copper coins were introduced by Sher Shah Suri?

questions.q: Who rebuilt/fortified Patna and made it the capital of Bihar in 1541 AD?

questions.q: The revolt of 1857 in Bihar was mainly led by which person?

questions.q: Which geological rock formation is the OLDEST hilly region of Bihar?
questions.explanation: The Dharwad rocks (found in Munger, Jamui, Nawada, Gaya, Rajgir) are the oldest hilly region of Bihar. Vindhyan rocks (Kaimur, Rohtas) are the second oldest.

questions.q: The region of West Champaran (Someshwar hills), being the newest hilly region of Bihar, belongs to which rock series?
questions.explanation: The Tertiary rocks (Pleistocene) form the area on the Someshwar hills in West Champaran — the newest hilly region of Bihar.

questions.q: Which district recorded the highest rainfall (204.7 cm) in 2023-24, and which the lowest (63.5 cm)?
questions.explanation: In 2023-24 the highest rainfall was recorded in Kishanganj (204.7 cm) and the lowest in Arwal (63.5 cm). The average rainfall of Bihar is about 112 cm.

questions.q: The river Ganga enters Bihar near which place?
questions.explanation: The Ganga enters Bihar near Chausa in Buxar district. Its total length in Bihar is 445 km, passing through 12 districts.

questions.q: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' and joins the Ganga at Kursela (Katihar)?
questions.explanation: The Kosi, notorious for changing its course and causing floods, is called the 'Sorrow (curse) of Bihar'. It joins the Ganga at Kursela (Katihar).

questions.q: Which river is also known as Narayani (in the plains)?
questions.explanation: The Gandak is also called Narayani, Sapta Gandaki and Shaligrami. Its main branch enters Bihar at Bhainsalotan (West Champaran).

questions.q: The Falgu (Phalgu) river of Gaya is formed by the confluence of which two rivers?
questions.explanation: The Falgu is formed by the confluence of the Lilajan (Niranjana) and Mohana rivers and joins the Punpun near Fatuha. Vishnupad temple lies on its bank.

questions.q: The Triveni Canal is constructed on which river?
questions.explanation: The Triveni Canal (part of the Gandak project along with Tirhut and Don canals) is on the Gandak river and irrigates West Champaran, East Champaran, Muzaffarpur and Vaishali.

questions.q: Which soil of North Bihar is found around the Someshwar range in West Champaran and is very fertile?
questions.explanation: The Piedmont soil is found around the Someshwar range in the north-west of West Champaran; it has high moisture and is suitable for paddy and sugarcane.

questions.q: Which is the ONLY National Park of Bihar, located in West Champaran?
questions.explanation: Valmikinagar National Park in West Champaran is the only National Park of Bihar (area 1779.71 sq km); it also contains the only tiger reserve.

questions.q: Which is the largest wildlife sanctuary of Bihar?
questions.explanation: The Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary (Rohtas-Kaimur), about 1784 sq km, is the largest wildlife sanctuary of Bihar.

questions.q: Which Bihar sanctuary is known as India's first dolphin sanctuary?
questions.explanation: The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary (Bhagalpur, ~60 km along the Ganga from Munger to Bhagalpur) is India's first dolphin sanctuary.

questions.q: As per the Forest Status Report 2023, the forest cover of Bihar is about what percentage of the state's geographical area?
questions.explanation: According to the Forest Status Report 2023, the forest cover of Bihar is 7532.45 sq km, about 8% of the total geographical area.

questions.q: Which doab lies between the Ghaghra and Gandak rivers in north Bihar?
questions.explanation: The three doabs of north Bihar are the Ghaghra-Gandak, Gandak-Kosi and Kosi-Mahananda doabs.

questions.explanation: Muzaffarpur leads in litchi production and Bhagalpur in banana production. Rohtas leads in guava and Darbhanga in mango.

questions.q: Which district of Bihar has the largest reserve of pyrite, containing 95% of India's reserves?

questions.q: Who is the constitutional head of the state government of Bihar?
questions.explanation: The Governor is the constitutional head of the state. The Governor is appointed by the President and holds office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.q: Under which Article can the Governor promulgate ordinances when the legislature is not in session?
questions.explanation: Article 213 gives the Governor the power to promulgate ordinances. Article 200 deals with assent to bills and Article 356 with President's rule.

questions.q: The legislature of Bihar is:
questions.explanation: Bihar has a bicameral legislature — the Legislative Assembly (lower house, 243 seats) and the Legislative Council (upper house, 75 seats).

questions.q: The Bihar Legislative Council is a permanent house; what fraction of its members retire every two years?
questions.explanation: The Legislative Council is a permanent house; one-third of its members retire every two years. Members serve a tenure of 6 years.

questions.q: Which Article governs the formation and creation of the State Legislative Council?
questions.explanation: Article 169 provides for the creation/abolition of the Legislative Council; its structure is described in Article 171. The Legislative Assembly is described under Article 170.

questions.q: The real executive head of the state who is appointed by the Governor is:
questions.explanation: The Governor appoints the Chief Minister (leader of the majority party in the Assembly) under Article 164. The Chief Minister is the real head of the state executive.

questions.q: Who administers the oath of office to the Chief Minister of Bihar?

options.D: Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.explanation: The Governor administers the oath of office and secrecy to the Chief Minister. The Chief Justice of the High Court is sworn in by the Governor.

questions.q: In Bihar, reservation for women in Panchayati Raj institutions is:
questions.explanation: Reservation for women is 50% in Panchayati Raj institutions (from 2006), 50% in urban local bodies (from 2007), and 35% in Bihar Police/other government services.

questions.q: Which Act provided the three-tier urban local self-government in Bihar (Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, Municipal Corporation)?
questions.explanation: The Bihar Municipal Act 2007 provides a three-tier structure of urban self-governance — Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council (Nagar Parishad) and Municipal Corporation (Nagar Nigam).

questions.q: What is the total number of Urban Local Bodies in Bihar at present?
questions.explanation: Bihar has 261 Urban Local Bodies — 19 Municipal Corporations, 88 Municipal Councils and 154 Nagar Panchayats.

questions.q: Who is the highest law officer of the state, appointed by the Governor under Article 165?

questions.explanation: The Advocate General, provided by Article 165, is the highest law officer of the state, appointed by the Governor; he may speak in the legislature but has no right to vote.

questions.q: The Patna High Court was constituted on which date?
questions.explanation: The Patna High Court was constituted on 3 February 1916. Its first Chief Justice was Sir Edward Maynard Des Champs Chamier.

questions.q: In which election year, after Jharkhand's separation (2000), did Bihar's Legislative Assembly seats become 243?
questions.explanation: After Jharkhand was separated on 15 November 2000, the number of seats in the Bihar Legislative Assembly remained at 243.

questions.q: Which miniature-painting style emerged in the 18th century in Patna blending Mughal, British and local styles?

questions.q: Which folk painting of the Mithila region, popularized by women, uses natural colours and includes forms like Aripan?

questions.q: Which folk art of the Bhagalpur (Anga) region is based on the folk tale of Bihula-Vishhari?

questions.q: Which folk song of Bihar is sung by young boys and girls during the month of Saavan?

questions.q: In which folk dance of Bihar do girls keep a perforated pot with a lit lamp on their head?

questions.q: Which folk drama, the work of Bhikhari Thakur, is presented by men assuming the forms of women?

questions.q: Which is the most important festival of Bihar, celebrated on the fifth and sixth day of Kartik month?
questions.explanation: Chhath Puja, the most important festival of Bihar, is celebrated on the fifth and sixth day of Kartik, worshipping the Sun and water.

1. Largest river of Bihar - Ganga
2. Largest city of Bihar - Patna
3. Largest airport of Bihar - Jayprakash Narayan Airport, Patna
4. Largest railway junction of Bihar - Patna Junction
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct: Ganga is Bihar's largest river, Patna its largest city, Jayprakash Narayan Airport (Patna) its largest airport, and Patna Junction its largest railway junction.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Which railway station in Bihar has the longest railway platform, and which bridge is the largest road bridge of Bihar?

options.A: Sonpur (longest platform); Mahatma Gandhi Setu (largest road bridge)
options.B: Patna Junction (longest platform); Mahatma Gandhi Setu (largest road bridge)
options.C: Sonpur (longest platform); Vikramshila Setu (largest road bridge)
options.D: Mahatma Gandhi Setu (longest platform); Sonpur (largest road bridge)

questions.answer_text: Sonpur (longest platform); Mahatma Gandhi Setu (largest road bridge)
questions.explanation: Sonpur has the longest railway platform in Bihar, while the Mahatma Gandhi Setu (across the Ganga) is the largest road bridge in Bihar.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Which fair is the largest fair of Bihar, and where is it held?
questions.explanation: The Harihar Nath fair, popularly known as Sonpur Mela, is the largest fair of Bihar, held at Sonpur.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Which was the first oil refinery of Bihar, and which was the first irrigation project of Bihar?
questions.explanation: Barauni Refinery was Bihar's first oil refinery, and the Son Multipurpose Project was Bihar's first irrigation project.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Which was the first planetarium of Bihar, and where is the second planetarium of Bihar located?
questions.explanation: The Indira Gandhi Planetarium in Patna is Bihar's first planetarium, and Darbhanga is home to Bihar's second planetarium.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding universities of Bihar:
1. Patna University (1917) was the first university of modern Bihar.
2. Nalanda Open University was the first open university of Bihar.
3. Magadh University is the largest university of Bihar.
4. Vikramshila University was established by King Dharmapala.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct: Patna University (1917) was the first modern university, Nalanda Open University the first open university, Magadh University the largest university (by affiliated colleges), and Vikramshila University was established by the Pala king Dharmapala.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Which was the first college of Bihar, and on what date was it established?
questions.explanation: Patna College, established on 9 January 1863, was the first college of Bihar.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Which district of Bihar is generally recorded as the hottest district in the state?
questions.explanation: Gaya district records among the highest temperatures in Bihar and is often cited as the hottest district of the state.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Which is the largest district of Bihar by area, and which is the smallest?
questions.explanation: West Champaran is Bihar's largest district by geographical area, while Sheohar is the smallest.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Who was the first Chief Minister of Bihar?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: Shri Krishna Singh.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian Governor of Bihar?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: Satyendra Prasanna Sinha.

questions.q: Who among the following was the first Governor of Bihar?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Sir James David Sifton.

questions.q: The first Hindi daily newspaper to be published in Bihar was
questions.explanation: Correct answer: Sarwa Hitaishi.

questions.q: India's first textile university will be set up in which of the following states ?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: Gujarat.

questions.q: World's first democratic republic is associated with which place of Bihar?
questions.explanation: The Lichchhavi republic of Vaishali is regarded as the world's first democratic republic.

questions.q: World's first university is regarded as:
questions.explanation: Nalanda University is called the world's first university. Aryabhatta is considered the world's first astronomer.

questions.q: Who was the first President of India, belonging to Bihar?
questions.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad of Bihar was the first President of India. Dr. Zakir Husain and Ram Nath Kovind were Bihar Governors who later became President.

questions.q: Who was the first Chief Minister of independent Bihar?
questions.explanation: Shri Krishna Singh was the first Chief Minister of independent Bihar; Mohammad Yunus (1937) was the first CM under British rule.

questions.q: Who was the first woman Chief Minister of Bihar?
questions.explanation: Smt. Rabri Devi was the first woman Chief Minister of Bihar. Bhola Paswan Shastri was the first Harijan CM, Mahamaya Prasad Sinha the first independent CM.

questions.q: The first Hindi newspaper of Bihar, 'Bihar Bandhu', was started in which year?
questions.explanation: 'Bihar Bandhu' (1874) was the first Hindi newspaper; the first English weekly was 'The Bihar Herald' (1875) and the first English daily was 'The Searchlight' (1918).

questions.q: Which was the first municipality of Bihar?
questions.explanation: Arrah was the first municipality of Bihar. The first English traveller to visit Bihar was Ralph Fitch (1587).

questions.q: Which is the largest road bridge of Bihar?
questions.explanation: The Mahatma Gandhi Setu is the largest road bridge of Bihar. Sonpur has the longest railway platform.

questions.q: Which is the largest fair of Bihar, held at Sonepur?
questions.explanation: The Harihar Nath (Sonepur) fair is the largest fair of Bihar. The first oil refinery is Barauni and the first irrigation project is the Son Multipurpose Project.

questions.q: Which district of Bihar is the largest (by area) and which is the smallest?
questions.explanation: West Champaran is the largest district of Bihar and Sheohar the smallest (by area).

questions.q: Which is the first university of modern Bihar, established in 1917?
questions.explanation: Patna University (1917) was the first university of modern Bihar. Nalanda Open University was the first open university and Magadh University is the largest.

questions.q: Which was the first college of Bihar, established on 9 January 1863?
questions.explanation: Patna College, established on 9 January 1863, was the first college of Bihar. The hottest and coldest district of Bihar is Gaya.
